title: Effects of age, sex, body weight, BMI, hand grip strength, diabetes, alcohol-and nicotine abuse on in-vivo human bone oxygenation
summary:
Monitoring of bone fractures is currently mostly done using X-rays. However, this has disadvantages: patients are exposed to radiation, and healing progress is often only visible much later because X-rays only show the calcium content, not the blood circulation which is crucial for healing. Since about one in ten fractures does not heal properly, we are looking for better methods. One solution is risk-free measurement using special light through the skin. In an initial study, we have already shown that this can be used to monitor healing and detect problems early, as oxygen levels in the bone's blood are particularly low when healing is impaired.
Before this light-based measurement can become a routine in hospitals, we need to clarify how personal characteristics affect the results. The aim of this study is therefore to find out what influence factors such as age, sex, body weight, smoking, alcohol consumption, or diabetes have on the measurement results. General physical strength is also taken into account. To do this, we perform painless measurements on the shin, radius, ulna, and collarbone. Only if we know how these factors change the values in healthy bone can we later reliably distinguish whether a patient's fracture is healing normally or not.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years (legal adulthood), No injuries, tattoos, or skin alterations at the sites to be examined, Written and oral informed consent (if capable of giving consent)
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to provide informed consent, Minority (under 18 years of age), Known pregnancy, Injuries, tattoos, or skin alterations at the sites to be examined
